open_questions: EP processing time: sources conflict (about 5 working days, 5-14 working days, within 20 working days, 3-8 weeks). Not confirmed on ESD.

The degree + 3 years experience rule was read in MIDA's guideline for manufacturing/selected-services 'term posts'. Whether ESD (most tech employers) and MDEC apply the same academic/experience rule to EP Category II was not confirmed.
Succession plan timing conflicts: one EY alert says Category II/III succession plans apply from 1 Jan 2027; other alerts say the requirement is postponed for GBS companies until 1 Jun 2027.
Salary-threshold concession reportedly applies only to MDEC-regulated companies (EY/KPMG via search). Its terms were not read.
Residence Pass-Talent (RP-T) eligibility (salary, years in Malaysia, degree) not found.
How a 3-year Indian bachelor's is treated: no explicit rule found. It is presumably a 'Degree' for the 3-year-experience tier, but this is unconfirmed.
EP fees and any employer levy not researched.
MYFutureJobs was unreachable from the research environment; its access method and robots stance are unknown.
DE Rantau: whether pass holders may work for Malaysian employers was not confirmed in an official text (assumed no; it is a remote-work pass).
Income tax rates and relocation norms not researched.

name: Malaysia

languages.note: English is widely used in tech, multinational and GBS (global business services) roles in Kuala Lumpur and Penang. Some ads ask for Malay or Mandarin; treat that as a filter signal.

salary.note: Levels.fyi Senior Software Engineer TOTAL COMPENSATION, 25th-75th percentile, from only 39 data points; median MYR 162K/yr (about MYR 13,467/month), 90th MYR 280,697. Levels.fyi notes that the percentiles may cover all levels; the all-level page gives a median of MYR 91.7K and P25-P75 of MYR 60,753-135,976 (155 salaries). The data skews to multinational and tech firms.

income_tax_note: Progressive resident income tax; 2026 rates not verified this session (see LHDN).
cost_of_living_note: Lower than Singapore; no figures researched.

visa_routes.name: Employment Pass (Category I / II / III)

salary_threshold.note: New policy in force from 1 Jun 2026 for new AND renewal applications. Cat I: at least RM20,000/month, 10-year tenure limit. Cat II: RM10,000-19,999, 10-year limit, replacement/succession plan required. Cat III: RM5,000-9,999 (RM7,000-9,999 for specific manufacturing sectors), 5-year limit, succession plan required. MIDA guideline: thresholds are BASIC salary excluding allowances and bonuses. A senior SWE would typically aim for Cat II or Cat I. The amount shown is the Cat III floor.

visa_routes.degree_requirement: MIDA guideline (manufacturing/selected-services term posts, 1 Jun 2026): Certificate, Diploma or Degree, with related experience of at least 7 / 5 / 3 years respectively. Key posts have no stated academic requirement. The ESD and MDEC equivalents were not confirmed.
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: No specific rule found. A 3-year Indian BCA should count as a 'Degree', which needs at least 3 years of related experience; a senior engineer with 7+ years meets this. Even read as a diploma-level qualification, 5 years of experience would suffice. Unconfirmed.
visa_routes.lottery_or_quota: No lottery. The employer needs approved expatriate posts. Tenure caps are 10 years (Cat I/II) and 5 years (Cat III).
visa_routes.path_to_pr: Residence Pass-Talent (RP-T) is the long-term option for expatriates; its criteria were not found. PR not researched.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: The employer applies. Before the EP it needs Labour Department (JTK) approval under Section 60K of the Employment Act and a MyFutureJobs advertisement for new term-post applications. The advert is exempt if basic salary is at least RM15,000, or for C-suite/key posts, corporate transfers and some other cases. Minimum paid-up capital (MIDA): RM250K Malaysian-owned, RM350K JV, RM500K foreign-owned. Fees not researched.

visa_routes.name: DE Rantau Nomad Pass (MDEC)

salary_threshold.note: Tech talent: at least USD 24,000/year (non-tech: USD 60,000). A Professional Visit Pass for remote workers, 3-12 months, renewable for up to 24 months total. Spouse, children and parents may accompany. Per the MDEC FAQ v10 via search results.

visa_routes.degree_requirement: None stated in the material found.
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: Not degree-gated in the material found.
visa_routes.path_to_pr: None. This is a temporary visit pass.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: Self-funded. Only relevant for someone already working remotely for a non-Malaysian employer; it is not a route into a Malaysian job (assumed, see open_questions).

sponsor_register.name: None found. There is no public list of EP-approved employers.
sponsor_register.how_to_use: Nothing to match against. A weak positive signal is an employer that is MDEC-regulated (Malaysia Digital status) or a GBS company, since salary and succession-plan concessions reportedly target these. No downloadable list of such companies was verified.

negative: only Malaysian applicants will be considered

ease_for_indian_nationals.rationale: Tech work is English-friendly and the EP rules are clear. A 7+ year engineer meets the degree + 3 years experience rule even with a 3-year degree. However, salary floors doubled from 1 Jun 2026 (Cat II now RM10,000+ basic). Cat II/III require a succession plan, and employers must clear a JTK approval and a MyFutureJobs advert first. Pay is well below Singapore's.

factors.degree_recognition: A degree with 3+ years of related experience is accepted (MIDA term-post rule). 3-year degree length is not singled out in the material found.
factors.processing_speed: Unclear; sources range from days to 8 weeks.
factors.quota_or_lottery: No lottery. Expatriate post approval, tenure caps and succession plans apply.
factors.employer_willingness: Common at MNC, GBS and MDEC tech firms. The 2026 salary rise may reduce willingness at the mid-level.
factors.attestation_or_paperwork: Passport with at least 12 months validity, employment contract, academic certificates. Attestation needs not researched.

relocation_norms: Not researched. Parse 'relocation package' from the job text.

scam_warnings: See the region-wide warnings in th.json and sg.json. Indian missions warn of fake 'IT/data entry/digital marketing/customer support' jobs in Southeast Asia that end in trafficking to scam compounds in Myanmar, Laos and Cambodia, usually routed through Thailand. Malaysia was not named in the advisories found.

A genuine Malaysian EP is applied for by the employer (ESD/MDEC/MIDA) after JTK approval. Offers that ask the candidate to enter as a visitor and 'convert later', or that charge the candidate EP or agent fees, are red flags.
App-detectable: employer not findable in the company registry (SSM, not verified as an API); chat-only recruiting; a stated workplace outside Malaysia (Thai border, Cambodia, Laos).
